body.statement: Given a supplied total order on \(V\), under \(r(G,s)\leq3\), every nonempty \(R\in\mathcal C(G,s)\) has size three and meets both \(P_s\) and \(T_s\). For an optimal \(y\) of the natural covering relaxation, every \(A_t\) is feasible for \(0<t<1/2\), and some breakpoint choice satisfies \(\sum_{v\in A_t}c(v)\leq2\operatorname{LP}(G,s,c)\leq2\operatorname{OPT}(G,s,c)\). Such a choice is found in polynomial time by the promised-rank enumerator using the supplied order.
body.justification: The parent-spouse crossing property improves the generic factor three for rank-three hitting set to the vertex-cover threshold two.
body.gap: Elahi and coauthors explicitly leave efficient MCID approximation as future work, and Akbari, Etesami, and Kiyavash give only logarithmic approximation in general and exact polynomial algorithms through residual size two.
body.consumer: Given the promised rank and a supplied vertex order, the theorem provides a deterministic warm start with an auditable factor-two guarantee for the existing ILP and WPMAX-SAT workflows.
body.proof_tex:
Fix the supplied total order on \(V\).  By Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}rank\mbox{-}three\mbox{-}promise}\) and Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}residual\mbox{-}rank}\), every \(R\in\mathcal C(G,s)\) has \(|R|\leq3\).  Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}minimal\mbox{-}residual\mbox{-}clutter}\) writes such an \(R\) as \(F\setminus\{s\}\) for a hedge \(F\).  Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}first\mbox{-}rank\mbox{-}boundary}\) gives \(|F|\geq4\), hence \(|R|\geq3\).  Therefore every clutter member has size exactly three.  The final clause of that theorem also yields
\[
 R\subseteq P_s\cup T_s,
 \qquad R\cap P_s\neq\varnothing,
 \qquad R\cap T_s\neq\varnothing,
 \qquad P_s\cap T_s=\varnothing.
\]

The feasible region of Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}covering\mbox{-}lp}\) is nonempty because the vector \(y_v=1\) for all \(v\in V^{-}\) satisfies every constraint.  It is a closed subset of the compact finite-dimensional cube \([0,1]^{V^{-}}\).  Hence the linear objective attains its minimum; Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}rational\mbox{-}lp\mbox{-}polynomial\mbox{-}time}\) additionally supplies an optimal rational solution in polynomial time after the constraints have been listed.  Fix such an optimum \(y\).

Let \(0<t<1/2\), and let \(A_t\) be the set in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}parent\mbox{-}spouse\mbox{-}rounding}\).  Suppose for contradiction that \(A_t\cap R=\varnothing\) for some \(R\in\mathcal C(G,s)\), and put
\[
 a=|R\cap P_s|.
\]
The preceding partition and \(|R|=3\) imply \(a\in\{1,2\}\).  Since \(R\) is missed, the two threshold definitions give the strict inequalities
\[
 y_p<t\quad(p\in R\cap P_s),
 \qquad
 y_b<\frac12-t\quad(b\in R\cap T_s).
\]
If \(a=1\), then
\[
 \sum_{v\in R}y_v
 <t+2\left(\frac12-t\right)
 =1-t<1.
\]
If \(a=2\), then
\[
 \sum_{v\in R}y_v
 <2t+\left(\frac12-t\right)
 =\frac12+t<1.
\]
Either inequality contradicts the constraint \(\sum_{v\in R}y_v\geq1\) in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}covering\mbox{-}lp}\).  Thus every \(A_t\) is a feasible intervention.

Let \(T\) be uniform on \((0,1/2)\).  Endpoints have probability zero.  For \(p\in P_s\), the event \(p\in A_T\) is \(T\leq y_p\), and for \(b\in T_s\), the event \(b\in A_T\) is \(T\geq1/2-y_b\).  Since \(0\leq y_v\leq1\), direct evaluation of the corresponding interval lengths gives
\[
 \Pr(p\in A_T)=\min\{1,2y_p\},
 \qquad
 \Pr(b\in A_T)=\min\{1,2y_b\}.
\]
No vertex outside \(P_s\cup T_s\) is selected.  Using \(P_s\cap T_s=\varnothing\), linearity of expectation, and the positivity of costs from Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}positive\mbox{-}rational\mbox{-}cost}\), we obtain
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E\!\left[\sum_{v\in A_T}c(v)\right]
 &=\sum_{v\in P_s\cup T_s}c(v)\min\{1,2y_v\}\\
 &\leq2\sum_{v\in V^{-}}c(v)y_v\\
 &=2\operatorname{LP}(G,s,c).
 \end{aligned}
\]
For every intervention \(A\) feasible in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}mcid\mbox{-}objective}\), its incidence vector is feasible for the covering LP and has the same objective.  Minimizing first over fractional vectors and then over feasible interventions therefore gives
\[
 \operatorname{LP}(G,s,c)\leq\operatorname{OPT}(G,s,c).
\]

The membership of a vertex in \(A_t\) can change only when
\[
 t\in
 \{y_p:p\in P_s\}\cup
 \left\{\frac12-y_b:b\in T_s\right\}.
\]
After retaining only values in \((0,1/2)\), these finitely many critical values partition the interval into finitely many nonempty open cells, and \(A_t\) is constant on each cell.  The critical values have Lebesgue measure zero.  If every open cell had cost strictly greater than \(2\operatorname{LP}(G,s,c)\), then the preceding expectation would also be strictly greater than that quantity.  Hence some cell, and therefore its rational representative evaluated by Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}parent\mbox{-}spouse\mbox{-}rounding}\), satisfies
\[
 \sum_{v\in A_t}c(v)
 \leq2\operatorname{LP}(G,s,c)
 \leq2\operatorname{OPT}(G,s,c).
\]

Finally, Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}promised\mbox{-}enumeration}\), instantiated with the supplied total order on \(V\), lists every LP constraint exactly once in polynomial time under the rank-three promise.  This uses the order furnished as part of the theorem's input and introduces no additional order.  Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}rational\mbox{-}lp\mbox{-}polynomial\mbox{-}time}\) solves the resulting rational LP in polynomial time.  There are at most \(2|V|\) displayed critical values, so sorting them and evaluating the rational representatives and critical values is polynomial.  The cheapest evaluated set has the claimed cost and is feasible by the argument above.
